title: Paper clay toadstool garden decoration
subtitle: A set of three toadstools for a windowsill or sheltered outdoor display, no kiln needed
excerpt: Paper clay air-dry toadstools are built from a dome cap and a cylindrical stalk, joined and dried, then sealed and painted. The cellulose fibres in paper clay prevent cracking on the curved cap. Finished sizes range from 6 to 10 cm tall. These sit in a garden pot or on an indoor shelf.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Paper clay air-dry construction.

glossaryTerms.definition: Air-dry clay reinforced with cellulose fibres that bridge joins and reduce cracking during drying of curved or sculptural forms
Fully air-dried; pale and lightweight, ready for sealing and painting
The joining method: roughen both surfaces, apply clay diluted with water, then press together firmly

content.text: is the right body for toadstool caps because the cellulose fibres handle the stress of a curved dome drying without cracking. Plain air-dry clay is more prone to surface cracks on a solid dome. A set of three in graduated sizes reads well together on a shelf or in a pot outdoors in dry weather.

materials.name: Clay slip (paper clay thinned with water)

content.text: Toadstool A: stalk 4 cm tall, 2.5 cm diameter; cap 6 cm diameter. Toadstool B: stalk 5 cm tall, 3 cm diameter; cap 7 cm diameter. Toadstool C: stalk 6 cm tall, 3.5 cm diameter; cap 8.5 cm diameter.
Roll a cylinder for each stalk to the stated diameter, slightly taller than the final height. Press the base flat on a board to give a stable foot. Allow to stiffen for 30 minutes.
Trim the top of each stalk flat with a fettling knife so the cap will sit level.
Roll a ball of paper clay for each cap. Press it gently into a dome shape: flat on the underside, rounded on top, with the stated diameter. The cap should be 2.5-3 cm tall at the centre.

Smooth the cap surface with a damp sponge, working in circular strokes. The cap edge should have a gentle downward curve , press the rim toward the table slightly with your fingers to create the characteristic toadstool overhang.

method: score the top face of the stalk and the underside centre of the cap with a needle tool, apply slip to both, and press together firmly. Allow the joined piece to dry on a flat surface for at least one hour before moving. The paper clay fibres bridge the join effectively.

over two to three days. Paint caps red with acrylic and allow to dry. Add irregular white spots , pressed from a flat-end brush or a pencil eraser , over the cap. Paint the stalks cream or white. Seal all surfaces with an outdoor-grade varnish or three coats of neat PVA for a weather-resistant finish.
Add a small woodland figure , hedgehog or snail , made from the same paper clay at the base of one toadstool.
Press the cap over an upturned bowl to get a flatter, more realistic toadstool shape.
Use a brown and tan palette instead of red for a woodland porcini look.

items.cause: Air-dry clay used instead of paper clay, or the cap was dried too fast in a warm room
items.fix: Paper clay is more resistant to dome cracking. Small cracks can be filled with fresh slip at leather-hard stage

items.cause: The join was not scored and slipped properly, or joined when both pieces were already too dry
items.fix: Re-join with fresh slip and a deeper score at leather-hard. If both pieces are bone-dry, use a strong adhesive (PVA or epoxy)

items.cause: The base of the stalk is not flat, or the cap is heavier on one side
items.fix: At leather-hard, trim the base of the stalk with a fettling knife until flat. Prop the piece slightly if needed until fully dry
